area: Phaser 3.90 performance (render flags, pooling, atlases/generated textures, Arcade physics) — adjudicated for a 2-fighter procedural-vector duel scene

item_verdicts.title: roundPixels silently defaults TRUE since Phaser 3.70 — set it explicitly to false to match the Flash sub-pixel vector look
item_verdicts.why: The central factual premise is stale by five minor versions. The 3.70 flip was REVERTED in Phaser v3.85.1: the official v3.85.1 release notes state verbatim 'The Game Config roundPixels property now defaults to false.' and 'The uRoundPixels uniform has been removed from the Single, Multi and Mobile vertex shaders.' I confirmed this against the version the repo actually pins (package.json: "phaser": "^3.90.0") by reading v3.90.0's own src/core/Config.js: `this.roundPixels = GetValue(renderConfig, 'roundPixels', false, config);`. So the repo is ALREADY running sub-pixel — rounding is OFF, and it is off by default, not by accident. The proposed ADAPT (add `render: { roundPixels: false }`) is a literal no-op, the stated mechanism (uRoundPixels shader uniform in the texture pipelines) no longer exists on 3.90, and the diagnosis 'the game is running with rounding ON without anyone having chosen it' is simply false. The repo-side observations are all real (src/main.ts has no render block; DuelScene createHudTexts places chi numerals at `.text(799 + i * 73.5, 497, ...)`; drawFighters repositions texts.nameplate/playerName every frame from worldToStage at DuelScene lines ~750/752) — but they support nothing, because the default they are premised on inverted in 3.85.1. Source #1 (3.70 release notes) says what is attributed to it, and issue #6509 ('Camera jitter when camera rounds pixels') is real and on-topic; they are just describing a behaviour Phaser has since removed.

item_verdicts.title: Bake the static arena Graphics into a runtime-generated texture (generateTexture) — the one atlas-adjacent idea that fits the invariant
item_verdicts.why: Sources survive verbatim: the official Graphics concepts page says 'Under WebGL the graphics data is decomposed into polygons. Both of these are expensive processes, especially with complex shapes' and 'If your Graphics object doesn't change much (or at all)... you will help performance by calling Phaser.GameObjects.Graphics#generateTexture. This will "bake" the Graphics object into a Texture'. Repo state confirmed: DuelScene.drawArena() does `const g = this.add.graphics()` in create(), emits the gradient sky, 5 mist ellipses, a canopy loop, bamboo rows, lanterns and letterbox strips, and never clears or redraws it; grep across src/ finds zero occurrences of generateTexture. The deferral ('only on a measured frame-time problem') is the right call. What fails is the invariant-compatibility argument, which quotes only half the rule.
item_verdicts.correction: src/game/CLAUDE.md's invariant is two clauses, not one: 'All art is procedural vector (Graphics), all audio is WebAudio-synthesized. No image/audio asset files, ever.' The item cites only the second clause ('bans image asset FILES, not runtime textures'). A generateTexture bake replaces the arena Graphics GameObject with an `add.image(...)` on the display list, which touches the FIRST clause. The art stays procedurally authored, so this is a defensible reading — but it is a rule interpretation, not a rule the item already satisfies. Treat the bake as requiring an explicit owner ruling or a one-line CLAUDE.md amendment ('runtime-generated textures from Graphics are permitted; asset files are not') BEFORE implementation, alongside the 55/55 gate re-run the item already flags.

item_verdicts.title: Texture-atlas advice: inapplicable — DuelScene has zero Sprites, and file atlases are banned anyway
item_verdicts.why: Survives every attack. I re-ran the grep myself over src/ for `Sprite|add\.image|atlas|generateTexture|physics|arcade`: zero hits, exit 0, no output — there is genuinely not one texture-based GameObject in the codebase, so texture-swap batch flushes (the exact problem atlases solve) cannot occur. The src/game/CLAUDE.md quote is exact ('All art is procedural vector (Graphics)... No image/audio asset files, ever.'). DuelScene's only display objects are Graphics (fx, hud, the arena g) plus the Text objects built in createHudTexts(). The REJECT is correct on both the mechanical ground and the invariant ground, and the item correctly hands the one legitimate variant off to the arena-bake item rather than double-counting it.

item_verdicts.title: Object pooling: the expensive pattern it prevents is already absent — FX records are plain JS objects, not GameObjects
item_verdicts.why: ALREADY_DONE holds against direct reading. DuelScene declares `interface Trail { points: readonly Vec[]; bornAt: number }` and `interface Droplet { x; y; vx; vy; bornAt }` — plain data, no Phaser types; spawnBlood pushes object literals into this.droplets and update() prunes redStrokes with a `.filter()` on bornAt. Every Text is built exactly once in createHudTexts() (combo, comboPlate, nameplate, playerName, the chi numerals) — nothing in the per-frame path creates or destroys a GameObject. EncounterScene line ~219 carries the predicted comment verbatim: 'Drawn as a scaling block per digit rather than a Text object'. I also checked the allocation scale the item hand-waved as '~a dozen': src/config/combat.ts has BLOOD_COUNT = 9 and BLOOD_COUNT_SEVERED = 16, so the claim understates nothing. Adding a pool here would be pure churn, as stated.

item_verdicts.title: powerPreference / batchSize tuning: no-op at this scene's load — leave defaults
item_verdicts.why: The conclusion is right and the repo grounding is right — src/main.ts pins `type: Phaser.WEBGL` with the comment 'WEBGL explicitly (not AUTO): the art direction relies on WebGL-only features (e.g. Graphics gradients). Failing loudly beats degrading silently.', which does close off the franzeus Canvas-switch finding; and the draw list (2 tessellated fighters, ≤16 droplets, HUD rects, sim.projectiles at DuelScene line 602) is nowhere near 4096 quads. But the grade-A source cited for the default VALUES does not contain them.
item_verdicts.correction: Do not cite https://docs.phaser.io/api-documentation/class/core-config for the default values — I fetched it and it documents roundPixels, antialias, batchSize, powerPreference and physics as options WITHOUT stating any default. Cite phaser v3.90.0 `src/core/Config.js` instead, which I verified directly and which does support every number claimed: `batchSize` default 4096, `powerPreference` default 'default', `antialias` default true (and, fatally for item 1, `roundPixels` default FALSE).

item_verdicts.title: Arcade physics settings: nothing to tune — the repo intentionally has no physics engine
item_verdicts.why: Verified independently rather than taken on trust. My own grep over src/ for `physics|arcade` returns nothing at all, and src/main.ts's GameConfig (read in full) contains only type/width/height/backgroundColor/transparent/parent/scale/scene — no physics block. The root CLAUDE.md invariant cited exists and is quoted accurately: 'Phaser scenes are render-only — they never own gameplay state; Sim (fixed 60Hz, injected mulberry32 RNG, no Math.random in core) owns everything.' The projectile claim also checks out: DuelScene line 602 is `for (const k of this.sim.projectiles)`, i.e. drawn from Sim state, not from a physics body. Adopting Arcade would indeed breach the render-only invariant and the deterministic seed harness.

item_verdicts.title: The one real per-frame hotspot in THIS scene is stroke segment count, not entity count — thin drag points at the input boundary
item_verdicts.why: The code half is the strongest item in the set and survives fully. strokePinched really does issue a fresh `g.lineStyle(); g.beginPath(); g.moveTo(); g.lineTo(); g.strokePath();` per segment inside `for (let i = 1; i < n; i++)`; pointermove really does push EVERY event up to `this.dragPoints.length < 2048`; and the double-draw is confirmed at DuelScene lines 563-583 — live drag twice (body+core), each redStroke twice, each blade trail twice. The docs quote backing 'complex shapes are expensive' is verbatim. What does NOT survive is the fidelity justification: BOTH cited ledger rows are being asked to prove something they explicitly disclaim.
item_verdicts.correction: Strike the '15 Hz content floor' from the justification entirely. COMBAT_MEASUREMENTS §00 ends with the opposite of what is claimed: 'This is a property of the *archival capture*, not necessarily of the Flash game (which likely ran 24–30 fps). It bounds what we can ever learn from video, not what the original did.' The new §S24-H verify-pass block (2026-08-12) reinforces this against exactly this style of argument: 'The 60 fps "4-frame content block" defence is VOID — that is a property of the capture (§00), not of the game.' Second, §S24-B caps rendered stroke LENGTH (120–280 px @1080 = 53–124 world px; HEAVY band corrected 146–260 → 146–~275 by the same verify block), which says nothing about point SPACING along the stroke — it cannot license decimation. Re-ground the item on §S24-B's actual build consequence instead, which is a fidelity fix that happens to cut segment count as a side effect: 'The lie the owner saw is RENDER-side: DuelScene draws the raw drag uncapped. Render the truncated polyline bold (+ optionally the excess as the faint tail).' Truncating the DRAWN polyline to reachFor(...) is ledger-mandated, touches only the render path, and leaves stroke.points fed to Sim.applyStroke untouched — whereas the proposed min-distance decimation mutates the array the Sim consumes and therefore carries determinism risk the ledger does not authorise.

overall_note: Seven items attacked: 1 REFUTED, 3 WEAKENED, 3 CONFIRMED. The headline kill is item 1, the only item flagged 'now' — its premise is a Phaser fact that expired in v3.85.1. The research agent read the 3.70 release notes correctly but never checked whether the flip survived to the pinned version; Phaser reverted `roundPixels` to false and deleted the uRoundPixels uniform in 3.85.1, and v3.90.0's src/core/Config.js confirms `GetValue(renderConfig, 'roundPixels', false, config)`. The repo already renders sub-pixel, so the one-line 'fix' plus gate re-run is wasted motion on a false diagnosis. Generalisable lesson: for a versioned dependency, a release note is evidence about the release it announces, not about the version installed — read node_modules/the pinned tag's source. Sourcing quality was otherwise good but not uniform: the Graphics concepts page and the 3.70 notes contain their attributed quotes verbatim and issue #6509 is real, while the core-config API page was cited twice for default values it does not state (values true, citation wrong). The three REJECT/ALREADY_DONE items are the most solid work here — I re-ran the greps and read the interfaces, config constants (BLOOD_COUNT = 9) and CLAUDE.md quotes myself, and all three hold exactly as written. Item 7 identifies a genuine, correctly-diagnosed hotspot but reaches for ledger rows as fidelity cover, and one of them (§00) explicitly disclaims the inference in its own closing sentence — a §00-misuse the ledger's new 2026-08-12 verify block independently calls out as VOID. Its remedy should be re-pointed at §S24-B's render-side truncation, which the ledger actually mandates and which avoids mutating the point array the Sim consumes.
